Etcetera KTC1730 credits the Piano Trio Op. 16 (1882) to Joseph Callaerts, not Ryelandt; Presto lists 'Callaerts: Piano Trio, Op. 16'. Wikipedia gives Ryelandt two piano trios (Op. 57, Op. 131). Callaerts's trio could be its own entry if he passes the track-record rule.
Two movements, 1915 (Etcetera track titles); Phaedra Vol. 80 gives 'Piano Trio No.1 in B Minor, Op. 57', 17:29 against Etcetera 18:38.
Three movements, 1944 (Etcetera track titles), 14:26.

Marimba and string quartet, 1993; Eclipse Quartet/Winant, New World 2013, 13:57.

Scoring and 1898 date hold, but the Naxos (Fine Arts Quartet, with viola) and Dabrin (Mozart Piano Quartet) recordings are of the composer's 1909 version for violin, viola, cello and piano (The Strad: 'piano quartet version'). Only a MusicBrainz listing of 'Harmonium Pearls' (Camerata Tokyo 2013) may have the harmonium version; performers unverified. Consider a separate entry for the piano-quartet version.
Durand print is titled 'Romance pour violon, piano ou harpe et orgue', so the harp alternative holds; Hauk recording (violin, harp, organ) runs 6:41. IMSLP dates composition 1866 (Wikipedia 1868).
Piano, organ, violin, viola or cello, 1865 (IMSLP, Wikipedia list). Recordings: Hauk (organ, harp, violin, viola, 4:13) and 'Harmonium Pearls' per MusicBrainz; floor evidence is thin but real.
